title: Composable approval microservices: PRD sketch for low-latency customer-managed network approvals
content:
Summary:
This is a working PRD sketch proposing a composable approval-gate architecture for Private deployments that treats approval decisioning, evidence bundling, and audit emission as small, independently-deployable services. The goal is to provide low-latency, policy-composable approvals for customer-managed networking changes while producing compact, queryable audit streams that meet enterprise compliance needs.

Context and problem statement:
- Customers operating Private (VPC / on-prem) deployments require rigorous, auditable approval workflows for network changes (eg. route updates, firewall rules, peering).
- Existing monolithic approval flows bake logic into a single control-plane component: slow, hard to extend, and fragile when customers need custom validations or local operator interventions.
- Audit logs are bulky and noisy. Customers ask for concise, actionable evidence bundles that can be ingested into SIEMs or kept as immutable legal artifacts.
- Operator experience varies: some customers want human-in-the-loop approvals; others prefer automated lemmas with fallbacks. We need a flexible, performant system that composes these needs.

Goals (what success looks like):
1) Modular approval primitives: implement at least three reusable microservices (policy-evaluator, evidence-bundler, decision-logger) that can be composed into end-to-end approval flows.
2) Latency SLO: average end-to-end approval decision (policy-evaluator + bundling + logging) < 200ms for automated checks; human-in-the-loop flows prioritized but target < 800ms for system-side processing (human wait times excluded).
3) Compact audit envelopes: produce an evidence bundle per approval <= 8KB compressed, suitable for fast storage and quick forensic queries.
4) Pluggable attestations: allow customers to supply an external attestor (webhook or signed token) that the system can verify and include in the evidence bundle.
5) Migration surface: provide an adapter to map current monolithic approval configs into the new microservice chain with minimal customer downtime.

Non-goals:
- Not building a full SIEM or long-term archive storage service. We will export to existing storage / SIEMs.
- Not solving UI for advanced analytics in first phase — operator kiosk will be minimal.

Personas:
- Platform Operator (customer): needs clear evidence and a small surface for delegating approval authority to team members.
- Redwood SRE / Operator: wants predictable, testable approval flows and minimal blast radius.
- Security/Compliance Reviewer: needs tamper-evident artifacts and compact queries for audits.
- Developer on Redwood Product: composes policies and builds integrations (e.g., policy-as-code).

High-level architecture (sketch):
1) Gateway: receives change request (REST / gRPC) with authenticated caller and optional customer-supplied context (ticket id, change window).
2) Policy-evaluator service: executes ordered policy chain (built-in + customer plugins). Returns pass / fail + rationale fragments. Supports Rego-style policy bundles or sandboxed JS predicates.
3) Attestation-adapter: calls third-party attestors (if configured) and validates signed attestations. Falls back to operator-approval step if attestation missing.
4) Evidence-bundler: composes a compact envelope (header metadata, canonicalized request diff, policy rationale snippets, attestor proofs, sampling hash). Serializes into canonical JSON-LD and applies delta compression.
5) Decision-logger: writes a short indexed record to the audit stream (event-sourced) and pushes the full compressed evidence bundle to object storage / customer-forwarder. Decision-logger also emits a digest to the immutable ledger (optional).
6) Operator-kiosk (UX): lightweight UI to view request summary, quick-approve/deny with optional comments, and to attach external artifacts.

Data contracts and audit format (principles):
- Evidence bundle should be machine-parseable, canonicalized, and signed by Redwood service keys.
- Keep the queryable index (decision-log) minimal: timestamp, request-id, actor-id, decision, policy-tags, evidence-digest, retention-class.
- For long-term retention customers can opt into an encrypted archive with a custody key they control.

Performance and economics:
- Expect microservices to be colocated on control-plane clusters; critical path should avoid cross-region hops for global customers.
- Cost profile: evidence bundles compressed and offloaded to tiered storage; decision-log kept in hot index for 90 days by default.
- Batching opportunities: for high-churn operator flows, support micro-batches of evidence ingestion to reduce downstream costs (configurable).

Security & compliance considerations:
- All services must authenticate with mTLS and use token least-privilege.
- Evidence bundles must carry a chain-of-custody: service-signature, policy-version, customer-key-hash (if used), and attestor-signature (if present).
- Provide optional WORM (write-once-read-many) export for customers with strict retention requirements.

Customer-managed networking-specific hooks:
- Network-diff canonicalizer: converts customer-provided objects (Terraform plan, BGP config snippet, firewall rule delta) into canonical diffs for inclusion in bundle.
- Preflight simulation callback: allow customers to register a simulation endpoint that gets called with the proposed change and returns a risk-score used by policies.
- Network-agent witness: optional lightweight agent that can sign a local evidence stamp to reduce remote call trust dependencies.

UX and operator flows (notes):
- Fast-approve keyboard flow: one-click approve from decision email / kiosk for pre-authorized roles.
- Escalation policy: configurable chains (eg. auto-approve during low-risk windows, require 2x approval for high-risk).
- Rollback action links: every approval record includes safe-rollback recipe (idempotent revert steps) generated by the system.

Migration plan (high level):
- Phase 0: implement decision-logger + evidence-bundler, enable shadow writes from existing approval path to start building corpus and alerts.
- Phase 1: pilot with 2–3 enterprise customers, introduce policy-evaluator + attestation-adapter as optional components.
- Phase 2: enable graceful cutover and deprecation of monolith; provide mapping tool for existing approval rules.

Acceptance criteria / success metrics:
- Pilot customers report < 250ms median automated decision latency and evidence bundle size <= 8KB (compressed) for 90% of events.
- Index query latency for last-7-days decision-log < 50ms for common filters (request-id, actor-id, decision).
- Zero critical security findings in 3rd-party audit of evidence signing model.
- Migration tool converts >= 95% of customer rules without manual edits for pilot customers.

Open questions / risks (working list):
- How do we handle policy determinism across versions? Need policy-version pinning and replay for audits.
- What is the canonical schema for network diffs that covers Terraform, CloudFormation, and vendor CLI outputs?
- Legal: retaining compressed evidence bundles under customer custody — need EULA addendum for custody and subpoena handling.
- Performance: evidence-bundler CPU cost if compacting large diffs; need heuristics and limits.

Next steps / short-term ToDos:
- Engineering spike: build policy-evaluator prototype with Rego + sandboxed JS fallback (owner: Owen). Target: 3-week spike.
- Security review: threat model for evidence signing and custody (owner: Priya).
- UX mock: minimal operator kiosk and email flows (owner: Maya).
- Data export contract: propose default index fields and S3 object layout for evidence bundles (owner: Carlos).

Notes to reviewers (informal):
- This is intentionally lightweight in UI and ops details — prefer to validate architecture and data contracts first.
- Look for duplication with existing attestation and approval PRDs — I tried to avoid repeating rollout mechanics but the artifacts will need to integrate.
- If customer pilots are green, next doc will expand on policy DSL and operator SLA matrix.

Revision history:
- 2025-11-05 initial draft (Nina)
- 2026-01-12 added performance targets and migration sketch (Owen)
- 2026-03-10 incorporated security review notes and compact-envelope sizing (Priya)

Triage labels: experimental | pilot-ready | requires-security-review

-- end of sketch --
